title: The wedding of Shiva and Parvati
hookLine: the bride's mother faints at the ash-covered groom; why Shiva, the auspicious one, and Parvati are the couple Hindu brides pray to
carry: shiva means auspicious, even covered in ash
tomorrow: why did the whole world become Shiva's chariot?

lines: IS THAT HIM? NO, A GUEST.
THEN THE GROOM COMES INTO VIEW.
cards: On the roof of the mountain king's palace, a mother waits to see her future son-in-law. Her name is Mena. Down the road comes the wedding procession, and it is splendid: gods in bright clothes, on fine mounts, with music.
Each time a shining figure goes by, Mena asks, is that him? Is that Shiva? And each time she's told, no, that's one of his guests.
Then the rest of the procession comes around the bend, and she gets her first look at the groom.

teach.h: THE GROOM: ASH, SNAKES, A BULL.
teach.b: In the Shiva Purana's telling, Shiva's own companions, his ganas, come behind the gods. Some have strange faces, some are like ghosts and goblins, some are howling and dancing.
In the middle rides Shiva on his bull, smeared with ash, snakes for ornaments, dressed like a man who lives in cremation grounds.
Mena faints. When she comes to, she's furious. She blames the sage Narada, who encouraged the match, and says she'd rather see her daughter dead than married to that.
She will not give her away.
Parvati doesn't defend herself by pretending Shiva is ordinary. She simply says she will marry no one else. She has already chosen.
The gods and sages plead with Mena. Shiva, the god who burned Kama for trying to move him, bends for his mother-in-law. He takes on a form of great beauty, adorned like a bridegroom.

Mena looks again, and this time she's delighted. The wedding goes ahead, and the whole mountain celebrates. Temple art remembers that face: Shiva as the handsome groom taking Parvati's hand is called Kalyanasundara.
But notice the name everyone was arguing about.
Shiva means the auspicious one, the kind, the blessed. The groom in cremation ash is, by name, good fortune itself. Mena saw the ash; Parvati saw who he was.

teach.h: THE MODEL COUPLE OF HINDU MARRIAGE.
teach.b: That's why Shiva and Parvati are the model couple of Hindu marriage.
In many families a bride prays to Gauri, which is Parvati, before her wedding, and girls pray for a husband like Shiva; many say that means a love that sees past the ash.

how: The wedding of Shiva and Parvati is retold in the Shiva Purana and other Puranas and honored in temple festivals and in Kalyanasundara images; in many families a bride prays to Gauri, Parvati, before her own wedding.

games.q: you're Parvati. your mother has fainted at the sight of your groom and now refuses the match. what do you do?
o: agree to marry someone more suitable.
say you will marry no one else.
ask Shiva to stay away until she calms down.
games.why: Parvati says plainly she has chosen and will marry no one else. then the gods plead, and Shiva himself shows a gentler face.

practice: Bring to mind someone your family sees only the ash of: a new partner from another background, an in-law, a neighbor whose ways are strange to you. Notice what you see first, the way Mena saw the ash.
Then ask what Parvati asked: who is this, really? If you pray, hold them before Shiva and Parvati, or God, in your own words. If you don't, just hold the question.

wordCard.voice: The Shiva Purana. Today's selection: the wedding, a mother who fainted at the groom, and a bride who saw who he was.

orig.note: Sanskrit: Parvati, the daughter of the mountain, Shiva's bride in today's selection.
